audience.text: Python developers building tools that parse, inspect, manipulate, or serialize HTML content using standards-compliant DOM and CSSOM APIs.

capabilities.text: Parse HTML strings, fragments, and files into a DOM tree using HTMLDocument.parse, HTMLDocument.parse_fragment, and HTMLDocument.load.
capabilities.title: Parse HTML into DOM

capabilities.text: Create, append, and remove nodes; read and write attributes, text content, and classes; query by ID, tag name, class name, and CSS selectors.
capabilities.title: DOM manipulation and querying

capabilities.text: Attach CSSStyleSheets, inspect rule types, and resolve computed styles for elements using the CSSOM surface.
capabilities.title: CSSOM styling and computed styles

capabilities.text: Parse and manipulate URLs with URL and URLSearchParams; detect character encodings from byte streams with detect_encoding.
capabilities.title: URL and encoding utilities

capabilities.text: Optionally execute JavaScript against a parsed DOM using JSContext backed by QuickJS.
capabilities.title: JavaScript execution bridge

capabilities.text: Use Tokenizer and TreeBuilder directly to implement custom parsing pipelines or inspect token streams.
capabilities.title: Low-level parsing control

capabilities.text: Access specialized HTMLElement subclasses such as HTMLInputElement, HTMLTableElement, and HTMLMediaElement with their defined properties.
capabilities.title: HTML element specialization

capabilities.text: Serialize complete documents, fragments, or individual elements back to HTML strings using serialise or XMLSerializer.
capabilities.title: Serialization to markup

limitations.text: CSS selector matching supports core Selectors Level 3 grammar; dynamic and legacy pseudo-classes raise NotImplementedError.
CSSRule.type and CSSRule.css_text are not implemented; concrete rule subclasses expose their own properties instead.
Form constraint validation and HTMLImageElement.decode are present on the API surface but not yet implemented.
The library builds internal layout structures but does not expose a public API for rendering documents to images or PDF.
JavaScript execution requires the optional quickjs extra and exposes a read-only DOM proxy; dynamic import() is not implemented.
Single-colon legacy pseudo-element forms are not parsed by the CSS selector parser.

problems_solved.text: Parsing raw HTML strings or files into a standards-compliant DOM tree using the WHATWG tokenization and tree-construction algorithms.
Applying CSS stylesheets and resolving computed styles for elements using the CSSOM surface.
Serializing DOM nodes back to HTML strings for output, testing, or further processing.
Detecting character encodings from byte streams using BOM and content-based sniffing.

product_summary.text: Aspose.HTML FOSS for Python is a free, open-source Python library implementing WHATWG HTML and DOM standards for parsing, querying, styling, and serializing HTML documents.

uncertainties: The exact set of CSS pseudo-classes that raise NotImplementedError in the matcher is not fully listed in the facts.
The behavior of HTMLDocument.load for non-file inputs is not demonstrated in examples.
Whether the layout module supports pagination or only single-page layout is not evident from the facts.
The scope of JavaScript execution (e.g., availability of fetch, setTimeout) is not specified.
The versioning scheme and compatibility guarantees for the public API surface are not stated in the facts.
The exact behavior of detect_encoding when multiple encoding indicators conflict is not detailed.
Whether the tokenizer supports streaming input or only complete strings is not evident.
The handling of HTML entities and numeric character references in parsing is not explicitly shown.

workflows.name: Parse and mutate HTML
workflows.text: Parse an HTML string into an HTMLDocument, create new elements, append them to the DOM, and serialize the result.

workflows.name: Apply and inspect computed styles
workflows.text: Attach a CSSStyleSheet to a Document, create an element with classes and IDs, and resolve the cascade to obtain computed style values.

workflows.name: Query elements by tag or selector
workflows.text: Select elements using get_element_by_id, get_elements_by_tag_name, or CSS selector helpers.

workflows.name: Work with URLs and query parameters
workflows.text: Parse a URL, modify its search parameters, and serialize the updated URL string.

workflows.name: Execute JavaScript against the DOM
workflows.text: Create a JSContext with a parsed Document and evaluate JavaScript that accesses DOM APIs.

workflows.name: Tokenize HTML directly
workflows.text: Feed raw HTML into the Tokenizer class and inspect the resulting token stream.
